content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint may not align with objective for atopic hand and foot dermatitis",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving an IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1 at week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective is to assess efficacy on skin lesions, but the IGA (hand and foot) is a physician global assessment, not a direct measure of lesion severity. The mTLSS (modified Total Lesion Symptom Score) is more specific to lesion morphology and is listed only as a secondary endpoint. This mismatch may lead to questions about whether the primary endpoint captures the intended construct.",
      "fix": "Consider using mTLSS as the primary endpoint or justify IGA as a validated measure for hand and foot dermatitis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for emollient use is burdensome and may cause screening failures",
      "quote": "At least 11 (of a total of 14*) applications of a topical emollient (moisturizer) during the 7 consecutive days immediately before the baseline visit",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring 11 applications of emollient in the 7 days before baseline is a high burden and may be difficult for patients to comply with, especially those with busy schedules or who are not accustomed to frequent moisturizing. This could lead to unnecessary screening failures and delays.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing the required number of applications or allowing a grace period for compliance."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for patch test reaction is overly broad and may exclude relevant patients",
      "quote": "Patients with a positive patch test reaction to one or more allergens (a score of 1+ or above according to International Contact Dermatitis Research Group [ICDRG] grading scale) in either a. the baseline patch test series OR b. extended baseline or supplemental patch test allergens if such additional testing is conducted by the investigator OR c. Personal products if testing with such products is conducted by the investigator AND Which is deemed to be clinically relevant in the view of the investigator as the current cause of the hand and foot dermatitis.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "7.2.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criterion excludes patients with any positive patch test reaction deemed clinically relevant, but the definition of 'clinically relevant' is subjective and may vary among investigators. This could lead to inconsistent application and potential amendments to clarify criteria. Additionally, the note that patients with documented ACD are excluded regardless of current relevance is even more restrictive and may exclude patients who could benefit from dupilumab.",
      "fix": "Clarify the definition of 'clinically relevant' and consider allowing patients with a history of ACD but no current exposure to the allergen."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for inadequate response to topical treatment is ambiguous",
      "quote": "Patients with documented recent history (within 6 months before the screening visit) of inadequate response of atopic hand and foot dermatitis to topical medication(s) or for whom topical treatments of atopic hand and foot dermatitis is medically inadvisable",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of 'inadequate response' is subjective ('as per clinical judgment of treating physician') and the documentation requirements may be difficult to meet. This could lead to variability in enrollment and potential amendments to clarify what constitutes adequate documentation.",
      "fix": "Provide more objective criteria for inadequate response, such as a specific IGA score after a defined treatment period, and standardize documentation requirements."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring may be insufficient for dupilumab in adolescents",
      "quote": "Male or female ≥12 years old at time of the screening visit.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol includes adolescents (≥12 years) but does not specify additional safety monitoring for this population, such as growth and development assessments, which are important for biologic therapies in pediatric patients. This is a gap in safety monitoring.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety assessments for adolescents, including growth parameters and sexual maturation, and consider a pediatric advisory board."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint for HECSI is only for patients with hand dermatitis, but inclusion requires hand and foot involvement",
      "quote": "For patients with hand dermatitis, percent change from baseline to week 16 in Hand Eczema Severity Index (HECSI) score",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The inclusion criteria require involvement of at least 2 anatomical areas, which could be both hands, 1 hand and 1 foot, or both feet. The HECSI endpoint is only for patients with hand dermatitis, but the study population includes those with foot-only involvement (if both feet are affected). This creates a subset analysis that may not be powered adequately.",
      "fix": "Clarify that HECSI will be assessed in all patients with hand involvement, and consider a separate endpoint for foot dermatitis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoint for EASI is only in patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body, but inclusion does not require this",
      "quote": "In patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body in addition to hands and feet;",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "4.1.4 Exploratory Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exploratory endpoint for EASI is only in a subset of patients, but the protocol does not specify how this subset will be identified or whether the study will be powered for this analysis. This could lead to underpowered exploratory analyses.",
      "fix": "Define the subset criteria clearly and consider whether to include all patients or only those with body involvement."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for skin protection measures may be difficult to verify",
      "quote": "Patients need to have been compliant with the skin protection measures (as outlined in Section 8.10.3) through the entire duration of the screening period (minimum of 4 weeks but lasting to a maximum of 8 weeks).",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Compliance with skin protection measures over a 4-8 week screening period is subjective and may be difficult to verify, leading to potential disputes and amendments. The protocol does not specify how compliance will be measured.",
      "fix": "Provide a clear definition of compliance and a method for documentation, such as a patient diary."
    }
  ]
}
